16: 
17: Analyze Dynatrace AI-detected problems including root cause identification, impact assessment, and correlation with logs and metrics.

21: ## Use Cases
22: 
23: ### 1. Active Problem Triage

25: - **Trigger:** "active problems", "what problems are open", "current issues", "availability issues"

27: 
28: ### 2. Root Cause Investigation

30: - **Trigger:** "root cause of P-12345", "what caused this problem", "which entity is the root cause"
31: - **Done:** Root cause entity identified with affected entity list and blast radius

33: ### 3. Problem Trending

39: 
40: ## Overview
41: 
42: Dynatrace automatically detects anomalies, performance degradations, and failures across your environment, creating **problems** that aggregate related alert, warning and info-level events and provide root cause and impact insights.
43: 
44: ### What are Problems?
45: 
46: Problems are automatically detected, software and infrastructure health and resilience issues that:
47: 
48: - **Automatically correlate** related alert, warning, and info-level events across services, infrastructure, frontend applications, and user sessions
49: - **Identify root causes** using causal analysis of Smartscape dependencies
50: - **Assess business impact** by tracking affected users and services
51: - **Reduce alert noise** by grouping related symptoms into single problems that share the same root cause and impact
52: - **Track problem lifecycle** from early detection through resolution
53: 
54: ### Event Kinds
55: 
56: The `event.kind` field (stable, permission) identifies the high-level event type:
57: 
58: | `event.kind` value | Description |
59: |---|---|
60: | `DAVIS_EVENT` | Davis-detected infrastructure/application events |
61: | `BIZ_EVENT` | Business events (ingested via API or captured from spans) |
62: | `RUM_EVENT` | Real User Monitoring events |
63: | `AUDIT_EVENT` | Administrative/security audit events |
64: 
65: `event.provider` (stable, permission) identifies the event source.
66: 
67: ## Problem Categories
68: 
69: Common `event.category` values:
70: 
71: | Category | Description | Example |
72: |----------|-------------|---------|
73: | **AVAILABILITY** | Infrastructure or service unavailable | Web service returns no data, synthetic test actively fails, database connection lost |
74: | **ERROR** | Increased error rates beyond baseline | API error rate jumped from 0.1% to 15% |
75: | **SLOWDOWN** | Performance degradation | Response time increased from 200ms to 5000ms |
76: | **RESOURCE** | Resource saturation | Container memory at 95%, causing OOM kills |
77: | **CUSTOM** | Custom anomaly detections | Business KPI (orders/minute) dropped below threshold |
78: 
79: ## Problem Lifecycle
80: 
81: ```text
82: Detection → ACTIVE → Under Investigation → CLOSED
83: ```
84: 
85: - **ACTIVE**: Currently occurring issues requiring attention
86: - **CLOSED**: Resolved issues used for historical analysis
87: 
88: ## Essential Fields
89: 
90: ### Common Field Name Mistakes
91: 
92: | ❌ WRONG | ✅ CORRECT | Description |
93: |---------|-----------|-------------|
94: | `title` | `event.name` | Problem title/description |
95: | `status` | `event.status` | Problem lifecycle status |
96: | `severity` | `event.category` | Problem type/category |
97: | `start` | `event.start` | Problem start time |
98: 
99: ### Correct Status Values
100: 
101: ```dql
102: // ✅ CORRECT: Use these status values
103: fetch dt.davis.problems
104: | filter event.status == "ACTIVE"   // Currently occurring problems
105: //     or event.status == "CLOSED"  // Resolved problems
106: // ❌ INCORRECT: event.status == "OPEN" does not exist!
107: | limit 1
108: ```
109: 
110: ### Key Fields Reference
111: 
112: ```dql
113: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 1h
114: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
115: | fields
116:     event.start,                          // Problem start timestamp
117:     event.end,                            // Problem end timestamp (if closed)
118:     display_id,                           // Human-readable problem ID (P-XXXXX)
119:     event.name,                           // Problem title
120:     event.description,                    // Detailed description
121:     event.category,                       // Problem type
122:     event.status,                         // ACTIVE or CLOSED
123:     dt.smartscape_source.id,              // The smartscape ID for the affected resource
124:     dt.davis.affected_users_count,        // Number of affected users
125:     affected_entity_ids = smartscape.affected_entities[][id],  // Array of affected entity IDs
126:     dt.smartscape.service,                // Affected services (may be array)
127:     dt.davis.root_cause_entity,           // Entity identified as root cause
128:     root_cause_entity_id,                 // Root cause entity ID
129:     root_cause_entity_name,               // Human-readable root cause name
130:     dt.davis.is_duplicate,                // Whether duplicate detection
131:     dt.davis.is_rootcause                 // Root cause vs. symptom
132: | limit 10
133: ```
134: 
135: ## Standard Query Pattern
136: 
137: Always start problem queries with this foundation:
138: 
139: ```dql
140: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 2h
141: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate) and event.status == "ACTIVE"
142: | fields event.start, display_id, event.name, event.category
143: | sort event.start desc
144: | limit 20
145: ```
146: 
147: **Key components:**
148: 
149: - `fetch dt.davis.problems` - The problems data source
150: - `not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)` - Filter out duplicate detections
151: - `event.status == "ACTIVE"` - Show only active problems
152: - Time range - Always specify a reasonable window
153: 
154: ## Common Query Patterns
155: 
156: ### Active Problems by Category
157: 
158: ```dql
159: fetch dt.davis.problems
160: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate) and event.status == "ACTIVE"
161: | summarize problem_count = count(), by: {event.category}
162: | sort problem_count desc
163: ```
164: 
165: ### High-Impact Active Problems (affecting many users)
166: 
167: ```dql
168: fetch dt.davis.problems
169: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate) and event.status == "ACTIVE"
170: | filter dt.davis.affected_users_count > 100
171: | fields event.start, display_id, event.name, dt.davis.affected_users_count, event.category
172: | sort dt.davis.affected_users_count desc
173: ```
174: 
175: ### High-Impact Active Problems (affecting many smartscape entities)
176: 
177: ```dql
178: fetch dt.davis.problems
179: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate) and event.status == "ACTIVE"
180: | filter arraySize(affected_entity_ids) > 5
181: | fields event.start, display_id, event.name, affected_entity_ids, event.category, impacted_entity_count = arraySize(affected_entity_ids)
182: | sort impacted_entity_count desc
183: ```
184: 
185: ### Specific Problem Details
186: 
187: ```dql
188: fetch dt.davis.problems
189: | filter display_id == "P-XXXXXXXXXX"
190: | fields event.start, event.end, event.name, event.description, affected_entity_ids, dt.davis.affected_users_count, root_cause_entity_id, root_cause_entity_name
191: ```
192: 
193: ### Service-Specific Problem History
194: 
195: ```dql
196: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 7d
197: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
198: | filter in(dt.smartscape.service, toSmartscapeId("SERVICE-XXXXXXXXX"))
199: | summarize problems = count(), by: {event.category, event.status}
200: ```
201: 
202: ## Root Cause Analysis Patterns
203: 
204: ### Basic Root Cause Query
205: 
206: ```dql
207: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 24h
208: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate) and event.status == "ACTIVE"
209: | fields
210:     display_id,
211:     event.name,
212:     event.description,
213:     root_cause_entity_id,
214:     root_cause_entity_name,
215:     affected_entity_ids = smartscape.affected_entities[][id]
216: ```
217: 
218: ### Root Cause by Entity Type
219: 
220: Identify which entity types most frequently cause problems:
221: 
222: ```dql
223: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 7d
224: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
225: | filter isNotNull(root_cause_entity_id)
226: | summarize problem_count = count(), by:{root_cause_entity_name}
227: | sort problem_count desc
228: | limit 20
229: ```
230: 
231: ### Affected entity is an AWS resource 
232: 
233: ```dql
234: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 24h
235: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate) and event.status == "ACTIVE"
236: | filter iAny(startsWith(smartscape.affected_entities[][type], "AWS_"))
237: ```
238: 
239: 
240: ### Infrastructure Root Cause with Service Impact
241: 
242: ```dql
243: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 30m
244: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate) and event.status == "ACTIVE"
245: | filter matchesPhrase(root_cause_entity_id, "HOST-")
246: | filter isNotNull(dt.smartscape.service)
247: | fields display_id, event.name, root_cause_entity_name, dt.smartscape.service
248: ```
249: 
250: ### Problem Blast Radius
251: 
252: Calculate entity impact per root cause:
253: 
254: ```dql
255: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 7d
256: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
257: | filter isNotNull(root_cause_entity_id)
258: | fieldsAdd affected_count = arraySize(smartscape.affected_entities)
259: | summarize
260:     avg_affected = avg(affected_count),
261:     max_affected = max(affected_count),
262:     problem_count = count(),
263:     by:{root_cause_entity_name}
264: | sort avg_affected desc
265: ```
266: 
267: ### Recurring Root Causes
268: 
269: Identify entities repeatedly causing problems:
270: 
271: ```dql
272: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 24h
273: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
274: | filter isNotNull(root_cause_entity_id)
275: | summarize
276:     problem_count = count(),
277:     first_occurrence = min(event.start),
278:     last_occurrence = max(event.start),
279:     by:{root_cause_entity_id, root_cause_entity_name}
280: | filter problem_count > 3
281: | sort problem_count desc
282: ```
283: 
284: ### Cause Category vs. Root Cause Entity
285: 
286: These are different questions — pick the right approach:
287: 
288: - **"What causes problems?"** / **"most common cause"** → Summarize by `event.category`
289:   (SLOWDOWN, ERROR, RESOURCE, AVAILABILITY, CUSTOM). Explain what triggers each category.
290: - **"Which entity causes problems?"** / **"root cause entity"** → Group by
291:   `root_cause_entity_name`. Lists specific services, hosts, or apps.
292: 
293: **Cause category breakdown** (use when asked about common causes, patterns, or types):
294: 
295: ```dql
296: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 30d
297: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
298: | summarize problem_count = count(), by: {event.category}
299: | sort problem_count desc
300: ```
301: 
302: Then for each category, explain what triggers it using the Problem Categories table and
303: cite specific entities from the tenant data as examples.
304: 
305: ## Problem Trending and Pattern Analysis
306: 
307: Track problem trends over time, identify recurring issues, and analyze resolution performance.
308: 
309: **Primary Files:**
310: - `references/problem-trending.md` - Timeseries analysis and pattern detection
311: 
312: **Common Use Cases:**
313: - Active problems over time with `makeTimeseries`
314: - Problem creation rate by category
315: - Recurring problem detection by schedule
316: - Resolution time trends and P95 duration analysis
317: 
318: **Key Techniques:**
319: - **`makeTimeseries`** vs **`bin()`**: Choose the right approach for lifecycle spans vs discrete events
320: - **NULL handling**: Use `coalesce(event.end, now())` for active problems
321: - **Peak hours analysis**: Identify when problems occur most frequently
322: - **Impact trending**: Track user impact changes over time
323: 
324: See `references/problem-trending.md` for complete query patterns and best practices.
325: 
326: ## Cross-Domain Problem Queries
327: 
328: ### Problems Associated with Kubernetes Clusters
329: 
330: Use `affected_entity_ids` or `dt.smartscape_source.id` to find problems related to Kubernetes:
331: 
332: ```dql
333: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 7d
334: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
335: | filter matchesPhrase(dt.smartscape_source.id, "KUBERNETES_CLUSTER")
336:     OR matchesPhrase(dt.smartscape_source.id, "K8S_")
337: | fields event.start, display_id, event.name, event.category, event.status,
338:     dt.smartscape_source.id, affected_entity_ids
339: | sort event.start desc
340: ```
341: 
342: Alternative: expand affected entities and filter for K8s entity types:
343: 
344: ```dql
345: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 7d
346: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
347: | expand entity_id = affected_entity_ids
348: | filter matchesPhrase(entity_id, "KUBERNETES_CLUSTER")
349:     OR matchesPhrase(entity_id, "K8S_")
350: | fields event.start, display_id, event.name, event.category, entity_id
351: | sort event.start desc
352: ```
353: 
354: ### Simple Problem Listing
355: 
356: List all problems from the last 24 hours (common request):
357: 
358: ```dql
359: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 24h
360: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
361: | fields event.start, event.end, display_id, event.name, event.category, event.status
362: | sort event.start desc
363: ```

365: ## Response Construction
366: 
367: ### Problem Cause Summaries
368: 
369: When summarizing problem causes, categories, or patterns, provide a **comprehensive
370: breakdown** across all standard categories present in the data: AVAILABILITY, ERROR,
371: SLOWDOWN, RESOURCE, and CUSTOM. For each category found:
372: 
373: 1. **Category name** and count of problems
374: 2. **What triggers it** — brief explanation (e.g., RESOURCE = CPU/memory/disk threshold
375:    exceeded; AVAILABILITY = service or entity became unreachable)
376: 3. **Specific examples** from the tenant's data (affected entity names, problem IDs)
377: 
378: Do not stop after the first two categories — users expect the full picture. Reference
379: the Problem Categories table above for trigger descriptions.
380: 
381: ### Analysis Results
382: 
383: When presenting query results:
384: - Include **entity names** (not just IDs) — but choose the efficient method:
385:   - **Few entities (< 5):** `get-entity-name` calls are fine
386:   - **Many entities:** Use `query-problems` tool which returns names directly, or
387:     include `root_cause_entity_name` / `entityName()` in the DQL query to resolve
388:     names inline. Avoid calling `get-entity-name` in a loop for 10+ entities —
389:     this can exhaust the tool call limit and return no answer at all.
390: - Provide **actionable recommendations** aligned to the identified causes
391: - Organize by frequency or impact for easy prioritization
392: 
393: ## Best Practices
394: 
395: ### Essential Rules
396: 
397: 1. **Always filter duplicates**: Use `not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)` to avoid counting the same problem multiple times
398: 2. **Use correct status values**: `"ACTIVE"` or `"CLOSED"`, never `"OPEN"`
399: 3. **Specify time ranges**: Always include time bounds to optimize performance
400: 4. **Include display_id**: Essential for problem identification and linking
401: 5. **Test incrementally**: Add one filter or field at a time when building queries
402: 6. **Filter early**: Apply `not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)` immediately after fetch
403: 
404: ### Query Development
405: 
406: - **Start simple**: Begin with basic filtering, then add complexity
407: - **Test fields first**: Run with `| limit 1` to verify field names exist
408: - **Use meaningful time ranges**: Too broad wastes resources, too narrow misses data
409: - **Document problem IDs**: Always capture and store `display_id` for reference
410: 
411: ### Root Cause Verification
412: 
413: - Always filter `isNotNull(root_cause_entity_id)` when required
414: - Cross-reference events using `dt.davis.event_ids`
415: - Consider time delays: root cause may appear in logs minutes before problem
416: 
417: ### Time Range Guidelines
418: 
419: ```dql
420: // ✅ GOOD - Specific time range
421: fetch dt.davis.problems, from:now() - 4h
422: ```
423: 
424: ```dql
425: // ❌ BAD - Scans all historical data
426: fetch dt.davis.problems
427: ```
428: 
429: ### Absolute Timeframes Require Double Quotes
430: 
431: When using absolute ISO 8601 timestamps for `from` and `to` in DQL queries, **always wrap them in double quotes**. Unquoted timestamps are a syntax error.
432: 
433: ```dql
434: // ✅ CORRECT - absolute timestamps quoted
435: fetch dt.davis.problems, from: "2026-05-18T22:50:00Z", to: "2026-05-18T23:35:00Z"
436: | filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)
437: | fields event.start, display_id, event.name, event.category, event.status
438: | sort event.start desc
439: ```
440: 
441: ## Troubleshooting
442: 
443: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
444: |---------|-------|----------|
445: | No problems returned | Using `event.status == "OPEN"` | Use `"ACTIVE"` or `"CLOSED"` — `"OPEN"` does not exist |
446: | Duplicate problems in results | Missing deduplication filter | Add `filter not(dt.davis.is_duplicate)` immediately after fetch |
447: | Wrong field name (`title`, `status`, `severity`) | SQL-like naming | Use `event.name`, `event.status`, `event.category` — see field name table above |
448: | `root_cause_entity_id` is null | Not all problems have identified root causes | Add `filter isNotNull(root_cause_entity_id)` when querying root causes |
449: | Query scans too much data / times out | Missing time range | Always specify `from:now() - <duration>` on the fetch command |
450: | `affected_entity_ids` is empty array | Problem has no mapped affected entities | Check `dt.smartscape.service` or `dt.smartscape_source.id` as alternatives |
